column2: Operational cadence, data source availability, and prioritization matrix for municipal transit & logistics

column4: Question
Where is every bus right now, and is it on time?
Which routes are most often late, and at what times of day?
Where and when do buses bunch together, arriving close together followed by a long gap?
What is the actual wait between buses at each stop compared with the schedule?
Which scheduled trips never run?
How much do snow days and storms reduce on-time performance, by route?
Which neighbourhoods are more than a 5-minute walk from frequent service?
Which areas have the most homes but the least transit service per resident?
Which roadworks and road closures cause the biggest bus delays?
Which routes are most crowded, and where are riders left behind?
Which route segments are consistently slow and could be optimized?
How reliable are ferries compared with buses?
How reliable is passenger rail service in and out of Halifax?
How much freight moves through Halifax by mode (port, rail, truck, air)?
How does port activity affect truck traffic and congestion downtown?
Where and when is taxi and ride-hailing demand highest, and does it fill gaps in transit?
Which truck routes carry the most traffic through the city, and where are the bottlenecks?
Where are warehouses clustered, and how far are they from major highways?
How do flight arrivals and departures drive ground transportation demand from the airport?
Where are the gaps in the bike lane and sidewalk network?
Which bus stops lack safe walking or cycling access?
How quickly are sidewalks and bike lanes cleared after snow?
Which roads and intersections are most congested, and when?
Where do collisions happen most, and what conditions are linked to them?
How long does each road closure last, and what does it affect?
How has traffic volume on major routes changed year over year?
Where is parking demand highest, and when?
Do park-and-ride lots increase ridership on nearby routes?
